books.title: Introduction to Algorithms
books.why: The standard reference and textbook for algorithms; rigorous, complete, and still the book everyone is measured against.

books.title: The Art of Computer Programming
books.why: Knuth's life work. Volumes 1–4B cover fundamental, seminumerical, sorting/searching and combinatorial algorithms with unmatched depth.

books.title: Algorithm Design
books.why: Teaches algorithm design as a way of thinking, with unusually clear treatment of greedy, divide-and-conquer, DP and network flow.

books.title: Algorithms
books.why: Practical, code-first algorithms with a superb companion booksite; the best bridge between theory and working implementations.

books.title: The Algorithm Design Manual
books.why: The 'war stories' and the catalog of algorithmic problems make it the book engineers actually reach for when stuck.

books.title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation
books.why: The clearest introduction to automata, computability and complexity; proofs that read like explanations.

books.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
books.why: The Dragon Book. Lexing, parsing, semantic analysis, optimization — the canonical compiler text for four decades.

books.title: Concrete Mathematics
books.why: The mathematics behind algorithm analysis, taught with wit and margin notes; the foundation for reading TAOCP.

books.title: Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach
books.why: The modern graduate complexity text, from P/NP to PCP and derandomization; the authors' draft is free online.

books.title: Principles of Model Checking
books.why: The definitive textbook on model checking and temporal logic — LTL, CTL, fairness, probabilistic systems — in one rigorous volume.

books.title: Programming Pearls
books.why: Short essays on thinking clearly about programs; the bit-vector sort and back-of-the-envelope chapters are legendary.

books.title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
books.why: MIT's legendary introduction to computation: abstraction, interpreters, and the metacircular evaluator. Full text free from MIT Press.

books.title: The C Programming Language
books.why: K&R. The book that defined how programming languages should be documented — terse, precise, and complete in under 300 pages.

books.title: The C++ Programming Language
books.why: The language from its designer; the 4th edition is the authoritative account of modern C++11 design and idiom.

books.title: C++ Primer
books.why: The most thorough C++ tutorial; the 5th edition remains the standard way to learn the language properly from scratch.

books.title: Effective C++
books.why: 55 specific ways to improve your programs and designs; shaped how a generation writes C++.

books.title: The Practice of Programming
books.why: Simplicity, clarity, generality — Kernighan and Pike on the craft, with examples in C, C++, Java, Perl.

books.title: Think Python
books.why: How to think like a computer scientist, in Python. Free, concise, and widely used as a first programming book.

books.title: Fluent Python
books.why: The book that turns Python users into Python programmers: the data model, protocols, iterators, concurrency, metaprogramming.

books.title: Pro Git
books.why: The official Git book — from basics to internals — maintained and free at git-scm.com.

books.title: Code Complete
books.why: An encyclopedic, evidence-based handbook of software construction; the most-cited practical programming book.

books.title: Clean Code
books.why: A handbook of agile software craftsmanship — naming, functions, comments, tests — that set the vocabulary for code quality.

books.title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
books.why: The Gang of Four. 23 patterns that gave object-oriented designers a shared language.

books.title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
books.why: Named and catalogued the small behavior-preserving transformations every good programmer makes; the 2nd edition uses JavaScript.

books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
books.why: From journeyman to master: DRY, orthogonality, tracer bullets, and dozens of habits that still define professional practice.

books.title: The Mythical Man-Month
books.why: Brooks's Law, the second-system effect, No Silver Bullet — essays on software engineering that have never stopped being true.

books.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
books.why: The big ideas behind reliable, scalable, maintainable systems: replication, partitioning, consistency, stream and batch processing.

books.title: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective
books.why: CS:APP. How hardware and OS shape program behavior — data representation, machine code, caching, linking, concurrency.

books.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
books.why: OSTEP. Virtualization, concurrency, persistence — a free, modern OS textbook that has become the default.

books.title: Modern Operating Systems
books.why: Tanenbaum's comprehensive OS text, with case studies of Linux, Windows and Android.

books.title: Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach
books.why: The Turing Award-winning authors' graduate text; introduced the quantitative approach to architecture design.

books.title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
books.why: The dominant networking textbook, starting at the application layer and working down.

books.title: Database System Concepts
books.why: The standard database textbook: relational model, SQL, storage, indexing, query processing, transactions.

books.title: Distributed Systems
books.why: Principles and paradigms of distributed systems; the 4th edition is free from the authors.

books.title: Advanced Programming in the UNIX Environment
books.why: APUE. The definitive guide to the UNIX system-call interface; Stevens's writing is the gold standard for systems books.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.why: AIMA. The most widely used AI textbook in the world, spanning search, logic, planning, uncertainty, learning and robotics.

books.title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
books.why: The foundational RL text — bandits, MDPs, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo, TD, function approximation — free from the authors.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.why: The first comprehensive deep learning textbook, from linear algebra foundations to research frontiers. Free online.

books.title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
books.why: Bishop's Bayesian treatment of ML — kernels, graphical models, EM, variational inference — now free from Microsoft Research.

books.title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
books.why: ESL. The statisticians' view of machine learning; the reference for regularization, trees, boosting and model assessment.

books.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
books.why: Murphy's modern, encyclopedic rewrite of Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective; free online.

books.title: Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms
books.why: Information theory and Bayesian inference taught together, brilliantly; free from the author.

books.title: Probabilistic Graphical Models: Principles and Techniques
books.why: The comprehensive reference on representation, inference and learning in Bayesian and Markov networks.

books.title: Machine Learning
books.why: The classic first ML textbook — decision trees, neural nets, Bayesian learning, PAC theory — still lucid.

books.title: Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
books.why: Learning theory made accessible: PAC learning, VC dimension, SGD, kernels. Free from the authors.

books.title: Multiagent Systems: Algorithmic, Game-Theoretic, and Logical Foundations
books.why: The standard text on multiagent systems — game theory, learning, auctions, logics of knowledge. Free from the authors.

books.title: Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control
books.why: The most complete graduate robotics text: kinematics, differential kinematics, dynamics, motion and force control, visual servoing.

books.title: Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics and Control
books.why: Craig. The classic undergraduate introduction to manipulator kinematics, Jacobians, dynamics and control.

books.title: Robot Modeling and Control
books.why: Rigorous yet approachable modeling and control of manipulators; the standard companion to Craig at the graduate level.

books.title: Modern Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
books.why: Screw theory and product of exponentials from the start; free PDF, videos and software make it the best modern entry point.

books.title: A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation
books.why: MLS. Lie-group kinematics, grasping and nonholonomic planning — the mathematical foundation of modern robotics, free from the authors.

books.title: Probabilistic Robotics
books.why: Bayes filters, Kalman and particle filters, localization, mapping and SLAM — the book that defined probabilistic robotics.

books.title: Planning Algorithms
books.why: The encyclopedic motion-planning text, from configuration spaces through sampling-based, differential and decision-theoretic planning. Free.

books.title: Principles of Robot Motion: Theory, Algorithms, and Implementations
books.why: Motion planning from bug algorithms to PRMs, potential fields, cell decomposition and SLAM, by the field's leading researchers.

books.title: Robot Motion Planning
books.why: The book that unified motion planning around the configuration space; the root of the field's modern literature.

books.title: Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms
books.why: Spatial vector algebra and the recursive algorithms (RNEA, CRBA, ABA) behind every modern robot dynamics engine.

books.title: Robotics, Vision and Control
books.why: Fundamental algorithms explained through runnable code (MATLAB and Python toolboxes); the best hands-on robotics text.

books.title: Springer Handbook of Robotics
books.why: The field's reference handbook — 80 chapters by the world's leading researchers across all of robotics.

books.title: Introduction to Autonomous Mobile Robots
books.why: The standard mobile-robotics textbook: locomotion, kinematics, perception, localization and planning.

books.title: State Estimation for Robotics
books.why: Batch and recursive estimation, matrix Lie groups and pose estimation, written for roboticists; free from the author.

books.title: Underactuated Robotics
books.why: MIT's course text on algorithms for walking, running, swimming, flying and manipulation; free, interactive, continually updated.

books.title: Robotic Manipulation: Perception, Planning, and Control
books.why: MIT's manipulation course text — geometric perception, grasping, motion planning, force control — free with runnable notebooks.

books.title: Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision
books.why: The bible of geometric computer vision: projective geometry, camera models, epipolar geometry, reconstruction.

books.title: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications
books.why: The comprehensive computer vision textbook, updated for deep learning; free from the author.

books.title: Dynamic Programming and Optimal Control
books.why: The authoritative two-volume treatment of DP and optimal control, from finite-horizon problems to approximate DP.

books.title: Abstract Dynamic Programming
books.why: DP as the theory of monotone contractive mappings; unifies exact and approximate DP. Free PDF from the author.

books.title: Convex Optimization
books.why: Recognizing and solving convex problems; the most influential optimization text of its era, free from the authors.

books.title: Numerical Optimization
books.why: The standard reference for continuous optimization algorithms: line search, trust region, quasi-Newton, SQP, interior point.

books.title: Feedback Systems: An Introduction for Scientists and Engineers
books.why: A modern introduction to feedback and control across disciplines; free and maintained by the authors.

books.title: Nonlinear Systems
books.why: The standard graduate text on nonlinear systems and Lyapunov stability theory.

books.title: Applied Nonlinear Control
books.why: Lyapunov, feedback linearization, sliding mode and adaptive control, written for practicing engineers — the robotics community's favorite.

books.title: Optimal Control Theory: An Introduction
books.why: The classic, gentle introduction to optimal control — dynamic programming, calculus of variations, Pontryagin's principle.

books.title: Optimal Control and Estimation
books.why: Optimal control and stochastic estimation in one coherent Dover volume; the LQG treatment is exemplary.

books.title: Model Predictive Control: Theory, Computation, and Design
books.why: The definitive MPC text — stability, robustness, numerical methods — free from the authors.

books.title: Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation
books.why: The reference on state estimation for tracking: Kalman filtering, IMM, data association, navigation.

books.title: Mathematics for Computer Science
books.why: MIT 6.042's free textbook: proofs, induction, graphs, counting, probability — the discrete math every CS student needs.

books.title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
books.why: Strang's famously intuitive linear algebra, paired with the MIT 18.06 lectures.

books.title: Introduction to Applied Linear Algebra: Vectors, Matrices, and Least Squares
books.why: Linear algebra as it is used in data science and control — least squares and its applications — free from the authors.

books.title: Introduction to Probability
books.why: MIT's probability text: clear, rigorous, and built around problem solving.
